advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the up-to-10s ls-remote probe on the best-effort read path (via pending_init_attaches_to_existing) is acceptable latency for uninitialized repos with an unreachable remote, or gate/shorten it.
evidence: Previously pending_init_attaches_to_existing was a purely-local ref check (`_git_ok(... rev-parse --verify ...)`) with no network I/O; the best-effort read path was non-blocking for uninitialized repos.
advisory.finding: pending_init_attaches_to_existing now performs a blocking network probe (git ls-remote, bounded to REMOTE_PROBE_TIMEOUT=10s) when no local or remote-tracking ref exists but a remote is configured. It is consumed by ensure_store_mounted_best_effort, which runs on the best-effort read path before in-process commands, so an uninitialized repo with a configured-but-unreachable remote incurs up to a 10s stall on every CLI invocation (e.g. `rebar search`/`show`) until the tracker is mounted. The 5.0s cache TTL only dedups within a single process, not across separate CLI invocations.
scenarios: A fresh clone whose configured origin is temporarily unreachable (VPN down, credential helper stalls): each `rebar` read command blocks ~10s before proceeding.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify no existing caller relies on `rebar init` silently ignoring extra argv tokens now that unknown options are rejected.
evidence: Prior behavior (diff): `silent = "--silent" in argv` / `return init_core(repo_root, silent=silent)` — no rejection of other tokens.
advisory.finding: init_cli now rejects any argv token outside {--silent, --force-new-store} with a nonzero exit, whereas it previously ignored unrecognized args (only `--silent` was inspected). This tightens the `rebar init` CLI contract and will now fail invocations that previously succeeded while passing an extra/unknown token.
scenarios: A script or wrapper that historically ran `rebar init <stray-arg>` and relied on it being ignored now exits 1.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update docs/architecture.md's auto-init section to describe the new bounded remote-advertisement probe and unreachable fail-closed behavior.
evidence: docs/architecture.md:243-245 `... it fabricates no new orphan history. So the auto-init gate does it automatically ... (discriminator rebar._commands.init.pending_init_attaches_to_existing)`
The updated predicate now additionally calls remote_exists + probe_remote_branch and classifies unreachable, none of which the architecture prose reflects.
advisory.finding: docs/architecture.md still documents pending_init_attaches_to_existing as returning true only when a tickets branch 'already exists locally or on origin' via a ref check, and does not mention the new bounded network advertisement probe or the unreachable/fail-closed behavior, so the architecture doc now drifts from the implemented discriminator.
scenarios: A maintainer reading architecture.md to reason about the auto-init gate misses the fail-closed network probe now embedded in the discriminator.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test invoking `init_cli(["--bogus"])` asserting return code 1 and the "unknown init option" stderr message.
evidence: ABSENT: `search_files` for "unknown init option" across tests returns no matches; no test passes an invalid flag such as `rebar init --bogus`.
advisory.finding: The new `init_cli` unknown-option rejection branch (returns 1 with an "unknown init option" stderr message) has no test; a regression that silently accepts or mis-handles an unrecognized flag would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a unit test: `assert init.init_cli(["--nope"]) == 1` and assert the captured stderr contains "unknown init option: --nope".

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests that run `init_core(repo, force_new_store=True)` against a repo with a pre-existing local `tickets` branch (and separately an `origin/tickets` tracking ref) and assert the "no effect" warning fires while the existing store is mounted.
evidence: init.py:388-389 `if force_new_store:` / `_warn_force_no_effect("the local ticket branch exists")`
init.py:396-397 `if force_new_store:` / `_warn_force_no_effect("the remote-tracking ticket branch exists")`

ABSENT: `search_files` for "local ticket branch exists" across tests returns no matches; existing tests cover only "the remote ticket branch is advertised" and "the reachable remote has no ticket branch" warnings.
advisory.finding: Two of the four `--force-new-store` "has no effect" warning branches are untested: the local-branch-exists and remote-tracking-branch-exists arms. Only the advertised-remote and reachable-absent warnings are asserted.
advisory.suggested_fix: Seed a local `tickets` branch (and a fetched `origin/tickets` tracking ref) in the host repo, call `init_core(repo, force_new_store=True)`, assert exit 0, tracker mounted, and stderr contains "no effect" with the branch-exists reason.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have the autouse fixture in test_init_fail_closed.py also call `_init_probe.clear_probe_cache()` so probe-cache state never leaks between tests.
evidence: _init_probe.py:34 `_CACHE: dict[...] = {}` is module-global with a 5.0s TTL (REMOTE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL), persisting between tests.
Only the four pure-`probe_remote_branch` tests (lines 241,265,272,287) clear the cache manually; the tmp_path-based in-process tests do not.
advisory.finding: The integration file's autouse `_reset_config` fixture does not clear the module-level `_init_probe._CACHE`; in-process tests (`pending_init_attaches_to_existing`, `init_core`, `probe_remote_branch`) leak probe-cache entries across tests, an isolation seam relying only on tmp_path key uniqueness to avoid cross-test contamination.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `_init_probe.clear_probe_cache()` to the `_reset_config` autouse fixture body (or a dedicated autouse fixture) so every test starts with an empty probe cache.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that initializes a host repo with NO configured remote and asserts `init_core(repo)` (without `--force-new-store`) exits 0, creates the tracker, and never issues an `ls-remote` probe.
evidence: _init_probe.py:61-68 `remote_exists` docstring: "No remote URL means there is no remote branch to protect, so callers may safely take the normal greenfield path without making a network request."
init.py:414 `if _init_probe.remote_exists(repo, remote_name, run_git_fn=run_git):` guards the entire probe block; the else (no remote) falls through to orphan creation.

ABSENT: `_host_repo` (test_init_fail_closed.py:35-42) always runs `_git(repo, "remote", "add", "origin", str(remote))`; no test constructs a repo without a remote, and `search_files` for "remote_exists" in tests returns no matches.
dropped.finding: The documented fail-OPEN greenfield path — a repo with NO configured remote (`remote_exists` returns False) — is never tested: it must skip the network probe and create an orphan store even without `--force-new-store`. The test helper always adds an `origin` remote, so this branch is unexercised.
dropped.suggested_fix: Build a host repo without `git remote add`, monkeypatch `run_git` to fail on `ls-remote`, and assert `init.init_core(repo) == 0` with the tracker directory created and the probe never invoked.
